questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Milan as my study destination for several reasons. First and foremost, I have always loved Italy – its culture, food, and overall lifestyle. Additionally, I knew many people who were also going to Milan or had been there before, which gave me a sense of reassurance and confidence in my choice. The city itself offers a fascinating mix of history, fashion, art, and an international atmosphere, all of which appealed to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Finding the necessary information upon arrival was moderately easy. The initial orientation meeting were very helpful in understanding the basics. However, the large amount of information was somewhat overwhelming, making it a bit confusing to navigate everything in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not recieve any help.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing was a bit challenging. However, we managed to find a great apartment through Spotahome, and our landlord was Italianway. The experience has been absolutely perfect - they have been incredibly reliable and helpful throughout the entire process. I would highly recommend them to anyone looking for housing in Milan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that finding off-campus housing in Milan can be expensive, and it’s crucial to start searching early. Using reliable platforms like Spotahome can help, and I personally had a great experience with Italianway, as they were professional and very helpful.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After accepting my exchange placement through the University of Copenhagen, I was automatically registered at the University of Milan.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I have been in contact with Daniel from Denmark and Massimo from Italy for assistance during the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I've changed classes several times due to schedule overlaps and because of the exams.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Course Registration Can Be Flexible – You might need to change courses due to scheduling conflicts or exam structures. If that happens, don’t worry - there is some flexibility, and you can usually adjust your courses within the first few weeks.

Reach Out for Help – If you have any doubts or issues, don’t hesitate to contact the international office or professors.

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: Masters only.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It varied a lot. In one course, "Learning and Development," we had to be very active and participate in the lessons. In most other courses, the teaching was more lecture-based, without exercises or interactive elements.

We had more classes and a wider range of subjects compared to Copenhagen, but fewer assignments and less reading.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Learning and Development 
- Business History 
- Digital Marketing and Innovation
- Governing the Future: Goals and Tools

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend Business History because it was very interesting and great to learn about Italian business history while being in Italy. The professors were also really good, dedicated, and helpful, which made the course even better.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rice, noodles, soy sauce, and generally any non-Italian ingredients were much more expensive than in Denmark. Additionally, rent was in general quite high.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Rice, noodles, soy sauce, and generally any non-Italian ingredients were much more expensive than in Denmark. Rent was also quite high. Additionally, eating out, drinks, and beer at clubs could be expensive.

On the other hand, wine was very affordable, and you could find high-quality leather jackets and other goods at local markets for a good price.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: highly recommend exploring the Saturday market in Navigli. Visiting Cimitero Monumentale (the Monumental Cemetery) is also a must.  Brera is an amazing area to walk around and eat. For trips outside the city, a day trip to Bergamo is a fantastic option. If you have a full weekend, a weekend trip to Bologna is definitely worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I loved the relaxed pace of life, the emphasis on enjoying good food, and the social culture. It was easy to adapt, as people were generally welcoming and open. The Italian way of life, with long dinners and a more laid-back approach to time, was something I really enjoyed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dog poops on the streets! :((((

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed pace of life - "Chill chill".

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't stress about courses and schedules – Things may seem chaotic at first, but people are very helpful, and everything will work out in the end. Flexibility is key!

2. Start looking for accommodation early – Housing in Milan is expensive and competitive, so it's best to start searching as soon as possible. Reliable platforms like Spotahome and agencies like Italianway can be helpful.

3. Embrace the Italian way of life – Enjoy the relaxed pace, take your time with meals, and don't expect everything to run on a strict schedule. It’s all part of the experience!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was experiencing a new culture and making great friends. I loved exploring Italian life, food, and traditions while creating unforgettable memories with amazing people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Taking exams by hand and without any aids.
